sections.heading: Problem bank — the spine of the content engine
sections.text:
Idea: Problem → Proof → Pipeline.
1. Collect real problems from clients, prospects, sellers and the community.
2. Solve one in public each month, anonymised and on the demo brand.
3. Turn each solution into content.
4. Route the person who sent it to a readout through their client manager.

The bank is also the dataset for the Q1 2027 research report.

sections.heading: Where problems come in
sections.text:
Source · How · Consent

Experience Day form · experience-day-nyc.md §1 · Q6 on the form
"Ask the account" (client managers) · ask-the-account.md · Client manager confirms; anonymised by default
Scorecard free-text · Last question on the AI-readiness assessment · Checkbox
Podcast/LinkedIn nominations · Nomination form (teaser arc, Dec) · Checkbox
Viva Engage / Beyond Pixels Q&A · Raquel logs them · Internal only unless the colleague agrees
"Hall of drift" submissions · Form + screenshot upload · Checkbox; screenshots redacted

Consent line (use everywhere): "Nagarro may use this problem, anonymised (no company, product or person named), in talks and content."

sections.heading: Columns (Excel/SharePoint list to start; move to a FigJam zone mirror)
sections.text: ID · Date · Source · Problem (1 line, anonymised) · Theme · Industry · Market · Estate size · Consent (anon / event-only / no) · Client manager · Status (new / answered / used in content / became a readout / became a deal) · Content links

sections.heading: Themes (tag one or two)
sections.text:
1. AI prototypes don't look like our product
2. Coding agents ignore the design system
3. Figma ↔ code drift
4. Token names AI can't read
5. Docs written only for humans
6. Several systems / multi-brand
7. Nobody owns agent changes (governance)
8. Accessibility (EAA) at scale
9. No people / no budget for the DS team
10. Proving ROI

sections.heading: Anonymisation rules
sections.text:
- No company, product, person or vendor names. Industry and region only, e.g. "a European bank".
- Rebuild every visual on the fictional demo brand. Never use client screenshots externally.
- Numbers are rounded or given as ranges.
- If two attributes together would identify the client (e.g. "the only Nordic lock maker"), generalise one of them.
- ASSA Abloy and any current-client work: never, even anonymised, until there is written clearance.

sections.heading: Monthly rhythm
sections.text:
- Week 1: pick the "problem of the month", the one tagged most often, with consent.
- Week 2: solve it at Beyond Pixels (internal) and record it.
- Week 3: publish it externally: 60 s clip + carousel + LinkedIn post.
- Week 4: written answers go to the submitters; client managers follow up.
- Quarterly: a "Top 5 problems" post and the roundtable agenda.
